name: Acmer P2 33W
tagline: Strong Acmer P2 tier: 33W compressed diode for faster work
tldr: Acmer P2 33W is the high-power open-frame Acmer before the enclosed P3. Verify real optical output vs marketing: capable cutter for the price when tuned properly.
mainObjective: Faster cutting and deeper hobby cuts while keeping solid engraving capability

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: 12 mm plywood in one pass at 100 mm/min (focus lowered 2 mm) on Acmer's P2-33W sheet
Faster cutting on common stock: 4 mm plywood at 500 mm/min and 5 mm MDF in one pass
Basswood engraving preset at 13,000 mm/min: ~12–18 min for our 10 × 10 cm photo test

editorialDepth.advantages: Acmer P2 33W targets mixed engraving and wood-cutting weeks: fewer passes on basswood and dark acrylic than weaker SKUs in the same line.
editorialDepth.limitations: Wrong pick if you never engrave and only wanted the lowest price. Ultra-fine photo work can look better on an engraving-first SKU. Open-frame: safety and smoke are on you.

cons: About $105 more than the 20W basic pack ($589 vs $484), and the 33W module alone costs $499
More smoke and heat at full power: the open frame needs an exhaust or the enclosure pack
Acmer's 'cut up to 30 mm wood' headline is not in its own sheet, which stops at 20 mm paulownia: anything thicker is multi-pass
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 33W SKU on Acmer P2. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Tune cut passes with air assist and focus checks. For photo engraving, slow down vs your cut presets: this head is optimized for throughput on wood, not only finesse.
primaryUse: Cut-biased diode tier for makers who outgrew 10–20W job times but stay on the same frame

faq.question: What does the Acmer P2 33W cut in a single pass?
faq.answer: Acmer's P2-33W sheet lists plywood at 500 mm/min (4 mm), 400 (6 mm), 300 (8 mm), 200 (10 mm) and 100 mm/min (12 mm, focus lowered 2 mm), all in one pass. It also gives 20 mm paulownia at 150 mm/min and 5 mm MDF at 200 mm/min. Black acrylic: 4 mm in one pass, 6 mm in 2, 10 mm in 4.

faq.question: Is the 33W rating real optical power?
faq.answer: Acmer sells it as a 33W compressed diode module; we have not measured its optical output ourselves. The manufacturer's own presets are consistent with a real step up from the 20W: 4 mm plywood at 500 vs 300 mm/min, and 10 mm plywood in one pass instead of two.

faq.question: Should I buy the 33W now or upgrade a P2 20W later?
faq.answer: Buy it now if there is a chance you will need it. On Acmer's store in October 2026 the basic packs were $484 (20W) and $589 (33W), a $105 gap, while the 33W upgrade module alone was $499. Refurbished units are also listed: $459 for the 20W and $527 for the 33W.

standoutFeatures.title: 12 mm plywood in one pass
standoutFeatures.body: Acmer's P2-33W sheet lists 10 mm plywood at 200 mm/min and 12 mm at 100 mm/min in a single pass, with the focus lowered 2 mm.

standoutFeatures.title: Shorter cut times
standoutFeatures.body: 4 mm plywood at 500 mm/min instead of 300 on the 20W, and ~6–10 min for our 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood.

standoutFeatures.title: Fewer passes on black acrylic
standoutFeatures.body: 6 mm opaque acrylic in 2 passes and 10 mm in 4, against 3 and 5 passes on the 20W (Acmer's figures).
